name: Issyk-Kul Biosphere Reserve
blurb: A high, salty mountain lake ringed by snow peaks, ibex and snow leopards.

tip.title: Thin out the ibex
tip.text: Ibex are the main prey of both wolves and snow leopards. Set Siberian ibex to -100% and watch the big cats shift to voles and ground squirrels, and the scavengers lose carrion.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Lake Issyk-Kul
nodes.desc: A huge, deep lake with no outlet. It is slightly salty (about 0.6%), so it rarely freezes even at 1,607 m, and it holds many wintering waterbirds.

nodes.name: Tian Shan meltwater
nodes.desc: Snowmelt and glacier streams from the surrounding mountains: about 118 rivers and streams feed the lake and water the valleys and shores.

nodes.name: Cold dry continental climate
nodes.desc: Cold winters and dry air shape the semi-desert, steppe and spruce zones, so water supply sets where plants can grow.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in mountain and shore soils, returned by decomposers, support plants from the shore to the spruce belt.

nodes.name: Soil bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Sea buckthorn
nodes.desc: Thorny shrub of riverbeds and valleys whose roots host nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Its berries are eaten by magpies and other birds.

nodes.name: Schrenk's spruce
nodes.desc: The main conifer of the Tian Shan forests, forming important stands above about 2,000 m.

nodes.name: Savin juniper
nodes.desc: Low evergreen shrub of dry slopes. Ibex browse juniper twigs in winter, and birds eat the cones.

nodes.name: Red clover
nodes.desc: Meadow legume of valley grasslands and shores, eaten by birds and grazers.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: Mountain goat of steep rocky slopes. Eats grasses and herbs, and in winter twigs and needles of trees such as spruce and juniper.

nodes.name: Kazakhstan vole
nodes.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of Tian Shan meadows, and a food source for many predators.

nodes.name: Relict ground squirrel
nodes.desc: Burrowing rodent of Central Asian mountains found in Kyrgyzstan, a plant eater and prey for raptors.

nodes.name: Ruddy shelduck
nodes.desc: Omnivorous duck of lakes and rivers that eats grasses, shoots, water plants and invertebrates. Breeds in Central Asia from March and April.

nodes.name: Eurasian magpie
nodes.desc: Omnivorous crow relative, the most recorded bird near the lake. Eats berries such as sea buckthorn along with insects and scraps.

nodes.name: Eurasian tree sparrow
nodes.desc: Small seed- and fruit-eating bird of villages and shrub thickets around the lake.

nodes.name: Black kite
nodes.desc: Opportunistic raptor that scavenges carrion and also takes fish, rodents and small birds.

nodes.name: Steppe rat snake
nodes.desc: Widespread snake of grasslands, shrubland and rocky ground up to about 3,580 m, taking small vertebrates.

nodes.name: Carrion crow
nodes.desc: Omnivorous scavenger and predator of small animals; also eats berries and seeds.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Pack-hunting predator of ibex and other wild and domestic animals, which also feeds scavengers with its kills.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: Elusive mountain cat. In the Tian Shan its main prey includes Siberian ibex and argali, and it also takes marmots and voles.
